title: A difficulty caused by one’s own act
odia: ଆପଣା ହସ୍ତେ ଜିହ୍ଵା ଛେଦି, କେ ଅଛି ତାର ପ୍ରତିବାଦୀ
literal_meaning: Having cut your tongue with your own hand, who is there to speak against it?
explanation: The sharp image points to trouble brought about by one’s own action. It challenges an attempt to shift responsibility elsewhere. It should not be used to assume that every hardship is self-caused or that someone who made a mistake no longer deserves help.
meaning_odia: ନିଜ କାମରୁ ନିଜର ଅସୁବିଧା ହେଲେ ଅନ୍ୟକୁ ଦୋଷ ଦେବା ସହଜ ନୁହେଁ—ଏହି ଭାବ କଥାଟିରେ ଅଛି। ତୀବ୍ର ଶାରୀରିକ ଚିତ୍ରଟି ନିଜ କାମର ଦାୟିତ୍ୱକୁ ଜୋର୍ ଦିଏ। କିନ୍ତୁ ସବୁ କଷ୍ଟ ନିଜ ଭୁଲ୍ରୁ ଆସେନାହିଁ, ଆଉ ଭୁଲ୍ କରିଥିଲେ ବି ସାହାଯ୍ୟର ଆବଶ୍ୟକତା ଶେଷ ହୁଏନାହିଁ।
usage_example: A team ignores its own backup plan, then finds that a preventable delay has stopped the work. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: The bodily injury is a rhetorical image, not an instruction. The final question is rendered as a challenge to protest; it is not evidence for a historical incident.

english_summary: The saying challenges someone to acknowledge trouble caused by their own actions, without blaming every hardship on its sufferer.
